transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

For weeks I’ve had this nonstop drive to take on more at the hospital, like I can’t slow my mind or body down even when I know it’s too much. It's gotten to the point where my supervisor and school counselor urged me to come get checked out because I just can't seem to pace myself.
Have you also been experiencing feelings of sadness, hopelessness, or irritability, or is it more that you're just feeling extremely energetic and driven all the time?

It’s actually a mix of both, and I swing between these two extremes. During my "high" phases, I feel ridiculously amped up, invincible, and easily irritated if anyone tries to slow me down. But now I've crashed into this heavy, sinking feeling of hopelessness and emptiness, where it feels like there's no point in even trying anymore.
Can you estimate how long these cycles of extreme energy and crashes into hopelessness have been happening, and how often do you switch between these two states?

This whole cycle of being extremely revved up and then crashing has been going on for about two months now, ever since I started night shifts and studying for my exams. I've been stuck in this really heavy, low phase for close to a month, starting right after I got written up at work.

Can you tell me more about how often you switch between these high and low phases, and do you recall having any similar episodes of extreme mood swings in the past, or is this the first time you've experienced something like this?

This is the very first time I've ever experienced anything like this; I've never had these kinds of mood swings before. It all started about two months ago when I began juggling night shifts and my CNA exams, which kept me super wired for a few weeks. But ever since I got written up at work, I've just been stuck in this heavy, exhausted low phase for close to a month now.

Can you clarify if you have had any periods of at least two weeks where you felt consistently extremely high or irritable, followed by at least two weeks of feeling consistently low, or have these episodes been shorter and more fluctuating?

Yes, they've definitely lasted for weeks at a time rather than shifting back and forth day-to-day. That high, wired phase went on consistently for about a month while I was juggling night shifts and exam prep. Since I got written up, this heavy, low phase has been dragging on every single day for close to a month now.

Can you confirm if you've had any periods where you switched from a high, energetic phase directly into a low, depressive phase without any significant time gap in between, or have there been gaps where you felt relatively normal before shifting into another extreme phase?

There wasn't any normal gap at all; I crashed directly from one extreme into the other. The moment I got written up at work, it was like a switch flipped and I went straight from being super wired and amped up into this heavy, exhausted low phase that I've been stuck in ever since.
Can you tell me if your current low phase, which has lasted for about a month, is the longest you've experienced, or have you had any longer periods of feeling extremely low in the past two months?

Yes, this current low phase is the only and longest one I've had in these past two months. The entire first month was that super wired, high-energy phase, and I only crashed into this heavy, low state about a month ago after getting written up at work.

Have you experienced at least two episodes of these extreme mood swings, with a period of at least two months of stability or normal mood in between, or has this been a single, prolonged cycle of highs and lows?

No, this has just been a single, continuous cycle that started about two months ago when I began juggling night shifts and exam prep. I had that intense high phase for several weeks and then crashed straight into this heavy low phase about a month ago, with no normal periods or previous episodes at all.
Have you experienced any periods of normal mood or stability that lasted for at least two months between episodes of extreme highs and lows, or has this been your first and only such cycle?

No, this is my very first time ever experiencing these kinds of highs and lows. The entire cycle only started about two months ago when I began juggling my new job and exam prep. Because of that, I haven't had any prior episodes or periods of stability between them.
Have you had any episodes of abnormally elevated or irritable mood that lasted less than two weeks, or have all your episodes so far lasted for several weeks at a time?

No, I haven't had any short episodes that lasted less than two weeks. The high, amped-up phase lasted consistently for about a month, and this heavy low phase has also been going on for close to a month now.
Can you confirm whether you have experienced any episodes of significantly elevated mood or irritability that did not last for at least one week, to help clarify the nature of your mood swings?
No, I haven't had any short-lived phases like that of just a few days. That high, irritable mood lasted continuously for about a month before I finally crashed into this low state.

You've mentioned that this is your first time experiencing such extreme mood swings, with a high phase lasting about a month followed by a low phase that's also lasted for close to a month. Can you confirm if you've had any other episodes of either extreme highs or lows outside of this single cycle that started two months ago?

Yes, I can confirm that. Before this cycle started about two months ago, I was always my usual calm and methodical self, and nothing like this has ever happened to me before. This is the absolute first time I've ever experienced these kinds of extreme highs or lows.

Have you experienced any symptoms or periods that could be considered a clear manic episode, lasting at least one week, or have all your high-energy phases been more on the hypomanic side, without causing significant impairment in your social or occupational functioning?

It was definitely a severe high phase that completely disrupted my life for several weeks. I got written up at work, missed shifts and classes, and isolated from friends because I was so out of control. During that time, I even started hearing a voice and truly believed the hospital was grooming me to overhaul their entire system, which made it impossible to function normally.
Can you tell me more about the voice you heard and the beliefs you had about the hospital during your high phase, such as how often you heard the voice and how strongly you believed in those ideas?

On a few nights when I stayed late charting, I heard a calm male voice telling me I was chosen to fix the system and that the patients personally depended on me. I was also completely, unshakably convinced that the hospital was secretly grooming me to lead a new program because they saw me as a genius, and no one could talk me out of it at the time. These voices and beliefs only happened during that super wired high phase, and they completely stopped the moment I crashed.
Did you experience any other psychotic symptoms, such as delusions or hallucinations, during your high or low phases, aside from the voice you heard and the beliefs about the hospital?

No, those were the only unusual things I experienced. I didn't hear any other voices or have any other strange beliefs, and those experiences only happened during that high phase and completely stopped once I crashed.
During your low phase, have you experienced any psychotic symptoms such as delusions or hallucinations, or were they exclusively present during your high phase?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that since I crashed. Those ideas about being chosen and the voice only happened during that super wired stretch when I wasn't sleeping. Once I hit this low phase, they completely disappeared.

Can you confirm if the psychotic symptoms, such as hearing voices and having delusional beliefs, occurred only during the manic or hypomanic episodes, or were they present at any point during your depressive episodes as well?

Yes, those experiences only happened during that high, super-wired stretch when I wasn't sleeping. Once I crashed into this low, depressed phase, they completely went away and I haven't had them at all.
